item.title: Cuvu College supports new rules, but are sticking to their own players for development
item.description: Navitalai Naivalurua · 05/08/2026 Cuvu College fully supports the new participation rules in the Vodafone Fiji Secondary Schools Rugby Union Competition, however, the school will not recruit six players from within its zone as it continues preparations for this Saturday's national quarterfinals.
item.content:encoded:
Navitalai Naivalurua · 05/08/2026

Cuvu College fully supports the new participation rules in the Vodafone Fiji Secondary Schools Rugby Union Competition, however, the school will not recruit six players from within its zone as it continues preparations for this Saturday's national quarterfinals.

Head coach Luke Salaba says there is no need to do so, as the team already has a number of talented 17-year-old players it intends to retain.

He says this will allow them to build on this year's experience and make an even greater contribution to next year's campaign.

Salaba says winning the Deans competition is a secondary objective, as their primary focus is on developing players into marketable athletes who can secure professional rugby contracts.

He says many of their players face academic challenges and may not excel in the classroom, so rugby provides them with a valuable pathway to a brighter future and greater opportunities.

The coach says the team's focus is firmly on maintaining discipline and improving the areas within its control.

He adds that, reflecting on previous campaigns, their biggest setbacks have often been self-inflicted. He says there have been occasions when the team has lost discipline, made costly errors, and lost focus during the quarter-final stages.

Cuvu College will face Nasinu Secondary School at 3.05pm on Saturday at Garvey Park in Tavua.

In another Under-18 quarter-final at Garvey Park, RKS will take on Ra High School at 1.40pm.

Meanwhile, at HFC Bank Stadium, Lelean Memorial School will face Ratu Navula College at 4.30pm, while Suva Grammar School will meet Ba Provincial Freebird Institute at 5.55pm.

item.title: MGM strengthens squad through transfer window ahead of Deans
item.description: Mahatma Gandhi Memorial High School has made use of the review of the Fiji Secondary Schools Rugby Terms of Participation to strengthen its squad ahead of the Vodafone Super Deans Championship. MGM coach Waliki Satakala says the school reached out to other schools like Marist Brothers High and Nasinu Secondary to improve its chances, with a player from Lami High set to join the side.
item.content:encoded:
Mahatma Gandhi Memorial High School has made use of the review of the Fiji Secondary Schools Rugby Terms of Participation to strengthen its squad ahead of the Vodafone Super Deans Championship.

MGM coach Waliki Satakala says the school reached out to other schools like Marist Brothers High and Nasinu Secondary to improve its chances, with a player from Lami High set to join the side.

Satakala says the decision was made as the team aims to build consistency ahead of the national championship as the school is also dealing with injuries picked up during the zone competition.

He says some players are not expected to recover in time.

Satakala says the transfer window had already closed, as it was open before the zone eliminations, prompting the school to act within the available timeframe.

He says the player joining from Lami is a hooker who has previously played alongside many of the MGM players through Suva Kaji Rugby and is also part of the athletics programme.

Speaking to fijivillage Sports about the Under-14 preparations, Satakele says Marist Brothers was kind enough to lend them some of their players.

He says MGM faces a difficult task in its opening Deans match against the defending champions, whose squad is made up mostly of Under-18 players.

Satakala says the team will do its utmost to manage the players it has available as it prepares for the challenge.

Meanwhile, he also says the school continues to place importance on both education and sport, with examinations scheduled from next Monday to Wednesday.

Satakala says MGM believes education and sport can co-exist, and the school is providing extra classes for students to help them balance their academic commitments with Deans preparations .

MGM High School will be represented in the U14 and U16 grade for the Deans competition, while their U18 girls will play in the Weet-Bix Raluve quarter finals.

The Deans National Quarters will be held at three venues for the first time this year.

Officials have confirmed that the three quarter finals will be held in Suva, Tavua and Savusavu.

item.title: George Bell ruled out of South Africa tour
Legge hopes Deans crowd backs Fijiana against South Africa this Saturday
item.description: Vodafone Fijiana XV Assistant coach Mike Legge is hoping rugby fans attending the Vodafone Super Deans Competition this Saturday at the HFC Bank Stadium will stay on to support the national women's team when they take on South Africa at 2pm. The Test match will follow the Deans fixtures, with Legge encouraging school rugby supporters and parents to remain at the venue and back the Fijiana side.
item.content:encoded:
Vodafone Fijiana XV Assistant coach Mike Legge is hoping rugby fans attending the Vodafone Super Deans Competition this Saturday at the HFC Bank Stadium will stay on to support the national women's team when they take on South Africa at 2pm.

The Test match will follow the Deans fixtures, with Legge encouraging school rugby supporters and parents to remain at the venue and back the Fijiana side.

Legge says the team's loyal supporters have continued to travel with them wherever they play and he expects them to turn out in numbers once again.

He also hopes parents and supporters attending the Deans competition will stay to cheer on the Fijiana, describing the Test as one that will showcase two very different styles of rugby.

On the field, Legge says t he team's biggest focus this week has been improving its physicality.

He says one of the biggest lessons from the Drua Women's Super Rugby Women's final loss to the NSW Waratahs in Lautoka was the importance of winning the collision.

Insert: Legge - Massive challenge July 04

Fijiana will face the Springbok Women at 2pm on Saturday at the HFC Bank Stadium, while their second Test will be held at Churchill Park in Lautoka next Saturday at 1pm.

item.title: Joseva Tamani signs with Highlanders till 2028
item.description: Former Swire Shipping Fijian Drua lock/loosie Joseva Tamani has just signed a two year contract with the Highlanders. Tamani, who left the Fijian Drua at the end of this season is signed till 2028 with the Otago side.
item.content:encoded:
Former Swire Shipping Fijian Drua lock/loosie Joseva Tamani has just signed a two year contract with the Highlanders.

Tamani, who left the Fijian Drua at the end of this season is signed till 2028 with the Otago side.

Also picked up by the Highlanders is Samoan international and former Moana Pasifika wing Tuna Tuitama.

Tamani made 13 appearances for Otago last NPC season, has signed on as a powerful addition to the Highlanders’ forward pack.

He is recognised for his explosive ball‑carrying, dominance in collisions, and exceptional mobility for a player of his size.

The 29‑year‑old brings significant experience, having already played 40 Super Rugby matches for the Fijian Drua and earned two Test caps for the FIJI Water Flying Fijians.

Tamani says he is excited to commit to the Highlanders and return to Dunedin.

He says tha t he really enjoyed his time with Otago last year and has grown to love the place.

Highlanders Head Coach Jamie Joseph says Tamani’s NPC form made him an obvious target.

Joseph says they liked what they saw in Tamani last year when he played for Otago, where he was strong in contact and broke defences with his strength of carry and athleticism.

He says above all, Tamani was a consistent performer throughout the NPC season, and he is experienced at Super Rugby level and his versatility will be important in a tough tournament like Super Rugby Pacific.

Both players will feature in this year’s NPC competition - Tamani for Otago and Tuitama for Counties Manukau, before linking up with the Highlanders ahead of the 2027 Super Rugby Pacific season.

item.title: Ugandan and Pakistani athletes missing after Commonwealth Games
item.description: Several athletes, including competitors from Uganda and Pakistan, have gone missing after competing at the Commonwealth Games in Glasgow, failing to return home with their respective teams. Police Scotland confirmed it had received reports of a number of athletes being "unaccounted for" following the conclusion of the Games on Sunday.
item.content:encoded:
Several athletes, including competitors from Uganda and Pakistan, have gone missing after competing at the Commonwealth Games in Glasgow, failing to return home with their respective teams.

Police Scotland confirmed it had received reports of a number of athletes being "unaccounted for" following the conclusion of the Games on Sunday.

Ugandan sports website NBS Sport reported that four members of the country's boxing team did not board their scheduled flight home.

A team member reportedly told the website that the athletes planned to apply for asylum in Scotland.

Meanwhile, Pakistan reported that boxer Qudratullah also failed to return home with his teammates.

Officials searching his room reportedly found that he was no longer there.

The issue follows similar incidents at previous Commonwealth Games.

After the 2014 Glasgow Games, several dozen athletes disappeared following the event, with some later seeking asylum while others vanished without explanation.

item.title: CFL reunites with McDonald's Fiji Coral Coast Sevens as media partner for landmark 15th tournament in 2027
item.description: The world's top invitational rugby sevens tournament is set to return bigger than ever in 2027, with Communications Fiji Limited, the parent company of FM96, LegendFM, VITIFM, Navtarang, Radio Sargam and fijivillage, rejoining forces with the McDonald's Fiji Coral Coast Sevens as its official media partner. The partnership was officially signed today ahead of the 15th edition of the tournament, ma
item.content:encoded:
The world's top invitational rugby sevens tournament is set to return bigger than ever in 2027, with Communications Fiji Limited, the parent company of FM96, LegendFM, VITIFM, Navtarang, Radio Sargam and fijivillage, rejoining forces with the McDonald's Fiji Coral Coast Sevens as its official media partner.

The partnership was officially signed today ahead of the 15th edition of the tournament, marking the return of CFL as the event's media partner.

McDonald's Fiji Coral Coast Sevens founder Jay Whyte says he is delighted to be working with CFL again, describing the company as an important part of the tournament's history.

Whyte says the renewed partnership will bring fresh ideas to better engage rugby fans and visitors while helping take the tournament to an even higher level.

He says the 2027 tournament from the 14th to the 16th of January, will maintain its 24-team men's format, with the $50,000 first prize again up for grabs.

Whyte confirms defending champions Yaro Chiefs, the New Zealand Sevens and Australia Sevens teams have already committed to the tournament, while the Chennai Bulls are expected to field both men's and women's teams.

He says the 2026 edition attracted a record number of international teams, and organisers are expecting another strong international lineup next year.

Whyte believes the Fiji Coral Coast Sevens has now established itself as the world's leading invitational rugby sevens tournament.

Insert: Whyte on Fiji Coral Coast 7s 4th Aug 26

He says the tournament gives Fijians a rare opportunity to watch some of the world's best sevens players and teams compete on home soil, despite Fiji not hosting an HSBC SVNS Series event.

Whyte also confirmed that the Mike Friday Select Team will return in 2027, giving fans another chance to watch elite international players up close.

CFL General Manager Charles Taylor says the company is excited to return as the tournament's media partner and is committed to delivering extensive coverage across all its platforms.

Taylor says fans can expect promotions across CFL's five radio stations, coverage on fijivillage, online videos and reels, news updates, as well as live entertainment, MCs and a sound system to enhance the tournament atmosphere.

Whyte also confirmed several major sponsors have already committed to the 2027 tournament, including naming rights sponsor McDonald's, Shangri-La as the women's division sponsor, GML through its Chery brand as the Bread Bank youth division sponsor, Tourism Fiji, Fiji Airways as the official airline, MOG UL, Sigatoka River Safari and Axellerate.

He says discussions are continuing with additional sponsors as preparations for the 2027 McDonald's Fiji Coral Coast Sevens gather momentum.

item.title: Stage set for Super Deans quarterfinals with defending champs RKS facing Ra High at Garvey Park
item.description: Navitalai Naivalurua · 04/08/2026 The stage is set for the Vodafone Fiji Secondary Schools Rugby Union Super Deans quarter-finals, with defending Under-18 champions Ratu Kadavulevu School taking on Ra High School at Garvey Park at 1.40pm this Saturday.
item.content:encoded:
Navitalai Naivalurua · 04/08/2026

The stage is set for the Vodafone Fiji Secondary Schools Rugby Union Super Deans quarter-finals, with defending Under-18 champions Ratu Kadavulevu School taking on Ra High School at Garvey Park at 1.40pm this Saturday.

The Fiji Secondary Schools Rugby Union Association has confirmed that the national Deans quarter-finals will be played across four venues: Suva, Tavua, Vatukoula and Savusavu.

The Under-18 quarter-finals will be played at two venues, with the second quarter-final at Garvey Park seeing Cuvu College take on Nasinu Secondary School at 3.05pm.

At the HFC Bank Stadium, Lelean Memorial School will face Ratu Navula College at 4.30pm, while Suva Grammar School will meet Ba Provincial Freebird Institute at 5.55pm.

People can check the full list of fixtures, venues and kick-off times on our website, fijivillage.
